answer: Onyx-key binding: each identity costs one ~$60 discrete TPM chip, since its address must be signed by a fresh manufacturer-certified endorsement key. Each epoch a verifier sends a random nonce; the chip must return it signed with an incremented monotonic counter within 1 s. The meadow registry hashes every endorsement key, so a reused or emulated chip collides or fails the cert chain and is rejected. Trust climbs a terrace of three such passes before payouts unlock. A farm cannot share chips: one key, one counter, one address.
